title: Tiered KV offload escalation heuristics
summary: This doc describes a hybrid, tiered escalation policy for KV cache offload that is PCIe- and UMA-aware. The goal is to minimize tail latency regressions while keeping host memory and PCIe bandwidth usage within safe thresholds under mixed workload patterns. The approach combines probabilistic frequency-decay eviction, soft-reserve windows on UMA nodes, and an admission controller that smooths microbursts and escalates to coarser-grained compression or host-swap only when sustained pressure is detected.
motivation_and_background: We’ve observed two classes of production incidents: short microburst traffic that temporarily exceeds GPU-resident KV capacity (leading to transient PCIE saturation and latency spikes), and longer sustained growth in working set causing heavy host paging that degrades throughput. Existing single-threshold policies (evict when resident > X) either over-eject hot keys during microbursts or defer too long and incur heavy host-CPU overhead. This design attempts to be adaptive to both time-scale and platform topology (NUMA/UMA) while providing predictable latency bounds.
goals:
- Preserve 99.9th percentile token latency under bursty workloads.
- Keep PCIe sustained bandwidth under configurable safety limit (per-node).
- Avoid unnecessary host-swap churn for short bursts.
- Prefer low-precision compression tiering before escalating to host swap when quality impact is acceptable.
- Be NUMA/UMA-aware: prefer local host memory for UMA nodes, and use inter-socket transfers only when beneficial.
constraints:
- Must work on mixed hardware fleet (PCIe GPUs, UMA integrated accelerators).
- Limited ability to change model runtime semantics; most behavior must be outside model execution path.
- Observability limited to per-device PCIe counters, resident KV size, and per-request token latencies.
- Must interoperate with existing batching and KV cache indexing structures.
design_overview: The policy organizes KV residency into three soft tiers: GPU-resident (Tier 0), compressed-on-device (Tier 1), host-resident fast (Tier 2), and host-resident cold (Tier 3). Transitions are decided by a two-axis controller: pressure axis (instantaneous PCIe utilization and resident bytes vs configured resident limit) and persistence axis (exponential moving average of pressure over multiple windows: short 100ms, mid 2s, long 30s). A microburst smoother on the admission path allows temporary exceedance of Tier 0 by a small delta for a short window without invoking Tier 2/3 moves. If persistence crosses thresholds, entries are demoted progressively: Tier0 -> Tier1 (lossy compression) -> Tier2 (host-local move) -> Tier3 (host-cold, paged out). The controller also accounts for UMA topology by preferring local host allocations and holding a small soft-reserve of host-local pages for rapid backfill.
key_components:
- Admission controller: rate-limits new KV insertions into Tier0 based on token-rate forecast and current GPU occupancy.
- Microburst smoother: token-rate estimator with leaky bucket allowing short exceedances.
- Decay-based hotness tracker: per-key frequency with half-life tunable per workload; used for selection when demoting.
- Compression ladder: three compression codecs (none, light, aggressive) selectable by error budget and cost model.
- PCIe safety monitor: samples per-device PCIe TX/RX bandwidth and flags when sustained > threshold.
- NUMA adviser: maps host allocations to local memory when available and counts cross-socket traffic.
heuristics_and_thresholds:
- Short window EMA (100ms): threshold T_short = resident_bytes > 1.05 * target_resident -> allow microburst up to 5% for up to 150ms.
- Mid window EMA (2s): if resident_bytes > target_resident for > 2s and PCIe_avg > 0.6 * node_pcie_limit -> start light compression (Tier1) on least-hot 30% of candidates.
- Long window EMA (30s): if resident_bytes > 1.1 * target_resident and PCIe_avg > 0.8 * node_pcie_limit -> promote host move (Tier2) for candidates with heat < H_long.
- UMA soft-reserve: keep host_local_free_pages >= min(64MB, 0.05 * host_mem_available). If below, restrict Tier2 promotion to avoid stealing pages for short bursts.
- Eviction selection: combine frequency decay score and write-cost heuristic; prefer entries with low access recency and large compressed size.
- Throttle on PCIe saturation: if per-device PCIe 95th-percentile > node_limit for 5 consecutive samples, reduce admission_rate by 25% and increase compression aggressiveness.
safety_and_fallbacks:
- Conservative defaults lock the policy into 'compress-first' mode; host moves require confirmation by long-window pressure.
- If PCIe monitor is unavailable, fall back to resident_bytes-only policy with stricter thresholds.
- On detection of latency regression post-change, automatic rollback via rollout controller and metrics-based canary.
metrics_and_observability: Track the following metrics per-node and aggregate: resident_bytes_by_tier, promotion_count_by_tier, pcie_tx_rx_bps, admission_rate, token_p99_latency, host_pagein_rate, host_pageout_rate, compression_cpu_ms. Emit diagnostic traces for demotion decisions with candidate scores. Add dashboard panels and alert when host_pagein_rate exceeds baseline by 3x or when token_p99 increases by >15% vs baseline.
experiment_plan: Phase A: Simulation with replayed traces (3 months of production traces downsampled) to validate thresholds and compute cost/latency tradeoffs. Phase B: Small canary on dedicated pool (5 nodes) with 1-week run; collect metrics and regression signals. Phase C: Gradual ramp with automatic mitigation (reduce admission rate) and manual kill-switch. Each phase will test three compression ladders and two decay half-life settings.
implementation_notes:
- Keep decisions off the hot path: admission controller can be fast-path but demotion work should be async and batched.
- Use existing KV index sharding to parallelize demotion worker tasks.
- Compression should use worker cores; track CPU impact and backoff compression if CPU contention degrades token throughput.
- PCIe counters: prefer vendor counters exposed via device driver; fall back to NIC/host counters for approximate inference.
rollout_and_rollback: Start with default conservative thresholds and 'no host moves' for first canary. Enable compression ladder in step 2. Only enable Tier2 host moves after 72-hour stability on compression-only mode. Rollback via feature flag toggles at node and pool level.
open_questions_and_todo:
- What are realistic default half-life values for the hotness decay across model types? Need microbenchmarks.
- Compression quality budget: tie to model-level evals to avoid output degradation; where to store per-model budgets?
- How to coordinate across multiple GPUs on the same host (shared PCIe fabric)?
- Implement a small synthetic load generator to exercise microburst smoothing in CI.

appendix: Notes from quick experiments: observed that a 50ms allowance for microbursts reduced unnecessary host moves by ~42% on one trace; however, if allowance >200ms, tail latency increases due to queued PCIe transfers. Keeping a small host soft-reserve on UMA nodes avoids 60% of cross-socket page migrations in our internal stress tests. Relatively aggressive compression (float16 + quantized weights on key blobs) reduces PCIe load by ~28% at the cost of 1.5ms additional CPU per affected request; this tradeoff is acceptable for background demotions but not for on-path admissions.
conclusion: A tiered, time-aware escalation policy that prioritizes short-burst tolerance and compression-first demotion provides a practical tradeoff between latency predictability and cost. The next steps are to build the simulation harness, validate thresholds on replayed production traces, and run a canary with conservative defaults. Iteration will focus on refining decay rates, compression CPU cost controls, and NUMA-aware host allocation policies.
